messages:
incident-bot: 🔔 INCIDENT ALERT — spike in 5xx and timeouts for /v1/generate across hosted region us-west-2. p95 latency jumped from 120ms -> 2.1s, p99 -> 12s. 502/504 rate ~8% over last 3m. Dashboard: https://redwood.internal/alerts/4391234567
deploy-bot: deployed commit 8f4c2b7 to service/inference at ~03:07 UTC (rolling). 
Jordan: paging oncall (I'm oncall now) — looking. @Maria can you pull perf traces?
Maria: on it. grabbing traces and tailing service logs.
Alex: I see the deploy — it included multiplexed connection changes to the gateway client (mux enabled). Could be related.
Samir: Customer ops: we have multiple customers reporting timeouts (billing and core product flows). Not widespread but high-value customers affected.
Jordan: ok initial triage: revert or throttle? Can we canary a rollback fast?
Alex: I can cut a rollback to previous deploy in 2–3m. if mux flag is culprit we can also flip feature flag `ENABLE_MULTIPLEXING=false`.
Maria: logs show a sharp increase in `pool_acquire_timeout` from the grpc-client to backend runtime. Example from host runtime-42:
```
ERROR timeout acquiring connection: pool_acquire_timeout after 5000ms
WARN request_id=abc123 latency=11000ms status=504 backend=runtime-42
```
Jordan: that suggests connection pool exhaustion after change. Does the new mux path increase concurrency per connection?
Alex: yes — multiplexing increases logical streams per connection; our connection pool code wasn't accounting for stream-level backpressure so pool sizes effectively dropped.
Lucy: if pool exhausted, immediate mitigation = disable mux and scale client pool. Which is faster?
Alex: flip flag first (low-risk) + roll back deploy in parallel. I'll flip flag for hosted region now.
oncall-bot: action: set featureflag ENABLE_MULTIPLEXING=false for us-west-2 — started by Alex
Alex: feature flag set — confirming traffic.
Maria: tail: error rate dropping at the edge. p95 back to ~180ms, p99 to ~2.1s, 5xx down to 1.2% (was 8%). Still seeing some retries.
Jordan: nice. Alex, still do rollback?
Alex: yes rolling back to commit 7a9e1f4 for service/inference to ensure stable run. Triggering now: `deploy rollback --service inference --to 7a9e1f4 --region us-west-2`
deploy-bot: rollback started (rollout id rback-439123). Estimated 4m.
Maria: followup: runtime logs show KV cache drains during rollback window, some long tail requests (~10–12s) but new requests stable.
Samir: customer-impact: notified top 5 customers via status; three reported transient errors and auto-retries recovered. We will add incident banner and proactive pings to SRE contacts.
Jordan: assign actions: Alex — post rollback + config diff; Maria — collect flame graphs and trace sample for postmortem; Samir — customer comms draft; Lucy — take next shift handoff at 07:00 UTC.
Alex: pushing rollback summary to runbook and linking the config diff: https://redwood.internal/repos/inference/commits/compare/7a9e1f4...8f4c2b7
Maria: collected traces: large queue times on client acquire path, traced to connection pool accounting bug. attaching sample trace id trace-4391 in diagnostics.
Lucy: taking over watch. brief summary for next oncall: mux caused pool accounting mismatch -> pool exhaustion -> increased timeouts/5xx. Mitigation: flipped feature flag, rolled back deploy, scaled pool as follow-up. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/connection-pool-exhaustion
Jordan: good. we should create a postmortem and tag eng-runtime, eng-sre, and product. Did we miss any customer-impact escalation?
Samir: customers tracked; no escalations opened yet. we'll surface RCA and ETA for mitigation steps.
Alex: follow-up immediate action items I will do today: (1) add guard in connection pool to account for multiplexed streams, (2) add canary that simulates high-vs low stream-per-conn, (3) tweak default pool size.
Maria: I'll prepare perf regression test in CI for multiplexing change.
Jordan: marking incident as mitigated. moving to postmortem. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: INCIDENT MITIGATED — 5xx/timeouts reduced to baseline. Root cause: connection pool accounting bug after multiplexing change. Follow-up: postmortem required.
Lucy: handoff note: oncall takeover at 07:00 UTC. I'll monitor for 2h then rotate to daytime oncall.
Samir: publishing status update to status.redwood.ai now.
Jordan: closing channel for active paging. leave follow-ups in #postmortems with links to traces and diffs.
